claims.claim_text: Archival finding aids and mission research support a high-confidence identification of Pierre Ravarre as the French radio operator also known as Jean Vernez.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The SHD finding aid names Pierre Ravarre, while the mission chronology links that distinctive name and alias to OSS Sussex operations.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match from the distinctive exact name, the index's French note and rank, an official individual-file pointer, and an OSS mission source.
claims.temporal_assessment: These sources document wartime service in 1943-1944 but do not identify a pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: The alias and radio role are identity evidence only. The separately found 1922 namesake was rejected because no reviewed source bridges him to this record.

claims.claim_text: An official naval history supports a high-confidence identification of indexed Commander Daniel Ravenel as Lieutenant Commander Daniel Ravenel Jr., USNR.
claims.evidence_excerpt: LCdr. Daniel Ravenel, Jr., USNR, was officer in charge of the Liaison Division.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history places Daniel Ravenel Jr., USNR, in charge of the Naval Command, OSS Liaison Division.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match based on the distinctive name, compatible naval rank, and direct OSS assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source establishes a wartime OSS assignment but not a pre-OSS civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: A postwar travel-agency reference was reviewed but was not used as evidence of pre-OSS employment.

claims.claim_text: Institutional and contemporary sources support a high-confidence identification of indexed Gregory S Razran as psychologist Gregory S. Razran.
claims.evidence_excerpt: During World War II, he also served as a statistical consultant to the U.S. Office of Strategic Services.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Queens College links the distinctive name to OSS statistical consulting, while TIME independently documents the middle initial and 1938 Columbia affiliation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match based on a distinctive full name, exact middle initial, direct OSS link, occupation, and consistent institutional chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Queens College source dates his professorship from 1940 and explicitly places his OSS consultancy during World War II.
claims.match_notes: The institutional chronology is internally coherent and independently corroborated by a contemporary article.

claims.claim_text: Gregory S. Razran was a psychology professor at Queens College from 1940 and also served as an OSS statistical consultant during World War II.
claims.evidence_excerpt: a psychology professor at Queens College from 1940 to 1972
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional biography dates continuous Queens College employment from 1940 and separately states that Razran served as an OSS statistical consultant during the war.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity match from the distinctive name, exact middle initial, occupation, and direct OSS statement.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: Queens employment began before OSS existed and continued during his wartime consultancy; the source does not say he left Queens.
claims.match_notes: Published as the best-supported immediate institutional affiliation, with the continuing-employment qualification explicit.

claims.claim_text: Queens College is the best-supported last civilian employer before Gregory S. Razran's documented OSS consulting service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: During World War II, he also served as a statistical consultant
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Queens College reports employment beginning in 1940 and describes OSS statistical consulting as an additional wartime role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity match from the distinctive name and direct institutional OSS statement.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded, but not an explicit 'left X to join OSS' statement; the source indicates concurrent college employment.
claims.match_notes: The claim is phrased as best-supported and retains the distinction between civilian employment and OSS consulting.

claims.claim_text: Gregory S. Razran held documented prewar lecturer and research-associate roles at Columbia University before joining Queens College.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Columbia University's Dr. Gregory S. Razran
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Queens College describes his lecturer and research-associate roles at Columbia, and TIME independently associates him with Columbia in April 1938.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match from the distinctive full name, exact middle initial, profession, and consistent institutional sequence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar affiliation ending when he joined Queens College in 1940; not presented as the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
claims.match_notes: This is an earlier academic affiliation and is excluded from immediate-employer analytics.
